title: Finite coefficient extension of a Tate algebra is ordinary tensor extension
statement:
For a complete field $F$ with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value and $r\geq0$, write $T_r(F)=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ for the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}c_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many $|c_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Let $K\hookrightarrow L$ be an isometric finite field extension of complete fields as above. Applying the inclusion to coefficients gives $\varphi:T_r(K)	o T_r(L)$. The map $$T_r(K)\otimes_K L\longrightarrow T_r(L),\qquad h\otimes\lambda\longmapsto\lambda\varphi(h)$$ is an isomorphism of $L$-algebras, where the tensor is the ordinary algebraic tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(h\otimes\lambda)(h^{\prime}\otimes\lambda^{\prime})=hh^{\prime}\otimes\lambda\lambda^{\prime}$. For every $K$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $L$, the constant series $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ form a basis of $T_r(L)$ as a $T_r(K)$-module via $\varphi$; in particular $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No separability assumption is made, and $r=0$ is included.

source.place: Conrad, Several approaches to non-archimedean geometry, Exercise 2.2.3(3) (analytic scalar extension); finite-degree ordinary-tensor specialization formulated by the agent using bounded coordinate projections in a finite-dimensional normed vector space. PDF p.13 read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix any $K$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $L$, and write $p_j:L\to K$ for its $K$-linear coordinate maps, so $a=\sum_j e_jp_j(a)$. The norm $|\cdot|_L$ makes $L$ a Hausdorff topological $K$-vector space: the scalar norm identity follows from the isometry $K\hookrightarrow L$, and addition and scalar multiplication are continuous by the norm inequalities. The domain has finite dimension and $K$ is complete and nontrivially normed. Thus [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] makes each $p_j$ continuous. Applying [lem-trf-continuous-linear-map-norm-bound] with $V=L$, $W=K$ and their absolute-value norms gives $C_j>0$ with $|p_j(a)|\leq C_j|a|$ for all $a\in L$.

proof.text:
For $f=\sum_
u a_
u x^
u\in T_r(L)$ set $f_j=\sum_
u p_j(a_
u)x^
u$. Given $\epsilon>0$, the set where $|p_j(a_
u)|\geq\epsilon$ is contained in the finite set where $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon/C_j$. Hence $f_j\in T_r(K)$. Isometry shows that coefficient inclusion $\varphi$ preserves the restriction condition. Coefficientwise addition and the finite Cauchy sums show that it is a unital ring map. Constants and finite sums of restricted series remain restricted: for addition use the union of the two exceptional sets, and for multiplication by a nonzero constant scale the threshold by its absolute value. Consequently $f=\sum_j e_j\varphi(f_j)$. If $\sum_j e_j\varphi(h_j)=0$, each coefficient is a $K$-linear relation between the $e_j$, so all coefficients of every $h_j$ vanish. Thus these constants form a $T_r(K)$-basis; the construction of $f_j$ is $T_r(K)$-linear since each coefficient of a product is a finite sum and $p_j$ is $K$-linear.

proof.text: Put $A=T_r(K)$, $B=T_r(L)$. The map $(h,\lambda)\mapsto\lambda\varphi(h)$ is $K$-bilinear, so [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives a $K$-linear map $\mu:A\otimes_KL\to B$ with the prescribed pure-tensor formula. Define $\eta:B\to A\otimes_KL$ by $\eta(f)=\sum_j f_j\otimes e_j$, using the coordinates just constructed. These coordinates are $K$-linear, so $\eta$ is $K$-linear. The coefficient expansion gives $\mu\eta(f)=f$. Conversely the $j$th coordinate of $\lambda\varphi(h)$ is $p_j(\lambda)h$, and bilinearity yields $\eta\mu(h\otimes\lambda)=\sum_j (p_j(\lambda)h)\otimes e_j=h\otimes\sum_j p_j(\lambda)e_j=h\otimes\lambda$. Pure tensors generate by the cited tensor-product statement, so $\eta\mu$ is the identity. This uses the ordinary algebraic tensor product throughout.

proof.text: For pure tensors, $\mu((h\otimes\lambda)(h'\otimes\lambda'))=\lambda\lambda'\varphi(hh')=(\lambda\varphi(h))(\lambda'\varphi(h'))$. Bilinearity and generation by pure tensors extend this equality to arbitrary pairs of tensors. Also $\mu(1\otimes1)=1$, and $\mu(h\otimes c\lambda)=c\mu(h\otimes\lambda)$ for every $c\in L$, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus the bijection $\mu$ is a unital $L$-algebra homomorphism, hence an $L$-algebra isomorphism.

proof.text: To verify flatness directly, let $u:N\to P$ be any injective $A$-linear map. The basis above identifies $N\otimes_AB$ with $N^d$: on a pure tensor send $n\otimes\sum_j b_je_j$ to $(b_jn)_j$, with inverse $(n_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j n_j\otimes e_j$. The first map is induced by an $A$-bilinear map, and the two compositions are the identity by the tensor relations and pure-tensor generation of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Use the identical formulas for $P$. Under these identifications $u\otimes\mathrm{id}_B$ is $(n_j)_j\mapsto(u(n_j))_j$, which is injective coordinatewise. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $B$ is flat over $A$ and $\varphi$ is flat. When $r=0$, the multi-index set has one element, so the same formulas give $K\otimes_KL\cong L$ and the given basis of $L$. No step uses separability or a trace pairing.
